observed: Wrote every .anvil/ path in FILE_CONTRACT.md and ROADMAP.md as a bare relative path, and listed anvil's own files and the files anvil creates in a user's repo in the same unlabelled list.
correction: There are two directory trees and the docs collapse them into one. Marketplace plugins are copied into ~/.claude/plugins/cache rather than run in place, so a bare .anvil/ is ambiguous and a command could read anvil's shipped files instead of the user's. Every path is written ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.anvil/...
proposed_line: Path rule — `grep -rn '\.anvil/' skills/ | grep -v CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` returns nothing

observed: MAP.md's example carried test:, build:, lint: and entrypoint: keys.
correction: All four are readable from package.json or equivalent, so they are exactly the 'could Claude have inferred this' case. Worse, they go stale, and a stale line is more dangerous than a lookup because Claude trusts it.
proposed_line: Flag a `CONFIG.md` key naming a build, test, lint or entrypoint command.

observed: Shipped process/scope.md carrying three seeded default lines that no correction in this repo had ever produced.
correction: Seeds are guesses. A guess occupying budget is worse than an empty file, because a guess gets believed and an empty file does not. Anvil may seed a file from what the user tells it, never from what anvil assumes.
proposed_line: Seed a context file only from what the user states, never from what anvil assumes.

observed: Wrote FILE_CONTRACT.md with its entire contents duplicated end to end, twice in two rounds, and did not check the file after writing it.
correction: Check wc -l on disk after a large write. A document that says 'this document is the authority' duplicated end to end would be a bad first impression.
proposed_line: Flag a file whose contents appear twice end to end after a rewrite.

observed: Ran Prettier over docs/, which pretty-printed three .jsonl spec examples into multi-line objects inside the section that requires one object per line, leaving the document contradicting itself.
correction: Add a .prettierignore or fence those blocks with prettier-ignore, then re-flatten them. This matters more than formatting usually would, because those examples are what someone copies when hand-writing M0's entries.
proposed_line: Flag a formatter run that reflows a fenced example whose spec requires one object per line.

observed: Committed and pushed the branch, then asked the user to open the pull request.
correction: You have access to gh, so next time open the PR yourself.
proposed_line: Open pull requests with `gh` rather than handing the step back.

observed: Stopped M3 to ask how six /scope runs should be executed, treating an installed-plugin session in a fresh context as a precondition for producing tickets at all.
correction: This is a meta framework and the package is markdown. The skill file is the instructions — follow them here rather than gating the milestone on a live run.
proposed_line: Anvil's own milestones are authored in this repo; do not gate progress on an installed-plugin run.

observed: User gave Claude Code feedback in ordinary conversation. It was written to Claude's own memory rather than to .anvil/feedback/, because every skill only captures during its own run and nothing captures outside one.
correction: There should be a feedback command that writes what I tell it into the logs.
proposed_line: Capture feedback given outside a command run, or the corrections that matter most are lost.

observed: /kickoff produced a TEST_CASES.md with more cases than the work warranted. The skill requires at least one case per acceptance criterion and /verify requires a verdict per case, so there is a ratchet upward and nothing pulling the other way.
correction: A lot of test cases that aren't needed in my case.
proposed_line: Generate test cases in proportion to risk, not one per criterion plus extras.

observed: The plugin was already installed at user scope, so the first real run skipped the install path entirely. Nobody has been through what a new user goes through.
correction: I didn't get the experience of installing this fresh because it was globally installed.
proposed_line: Exercise the install path from a clean state before claiming it works.

observed: The distilling command wrote context-file lines on its own once a lesson hit two sightings, asking only for CLAUDE.md proposals and evictions.
correction: Improve should only recommend to the human, to prevent AI slop or overfitting.
proposed_line: Recommend every context-file change and write nothing the user has not approved in that run.
